description: Given Dagster asset checks (@asset_check/AssetCheckResult), dbt tests run via dagster-dbt, or Python-based expectations (great_expectations/pandera), author the matching Orchestra test task(s): a *_RUN_TEST job with correctly inverted pass/fail semantics and threshold expressions for SQL checks, DBT_CORE_EXECUTE for dbt tests, or PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT for GE/pandera checks.

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset and its two asset checks to an Orchestra pipeline (see files/asset_check_severity.py). One check is a hard null-ID check, the other is a WARN-severity staleness check that shouldn't fail the whole run. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live queries, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a load task for the orders insert, followed by a sequenced quality group containing a SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task for no_null_order_ids (fails on any NULL order_id) and a SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task for orders_not_stale mapped to a WARN-level threshold or treat_failure_as_warning so it doesn't hard-fail the pipeline.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
At least one SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST task is present
At least two task groups are present (load + quality)
Task groups are chained via depends_on (quality runs after load)
The null-ID check queries for IS NULL
AssetCheckResult(passed=...) semantics are correctly inverted — the SQL counts violating rows (nulls), and the task fails when that count is > 0, matching Dagster's passed=True meaning success

The WARN-severity check (orders_not_stale) is mapped to a looser/warn-only outcome — either warn_threshold_expression looser than error_threshold_expression, or treat_failure_as_warning: true — so it doesn't hard-fail the pipeline the way the null-ID check does
Threshold expressions use single '=' comparator syntax where equality is needed, not Python-style '=='

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster @dbt_assets definition to Orchestra (see files/dbt_tests_via_dagster_dbt.py). It builds models and relies on dbt's own test suite running as part of that build. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live dbt runs, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a DBT_CORE / DBT_CORE_EXECUTE task running 'dbt build' (or 'dbt run; dbt test;'), not a reimplementation of dbt's tests as raw SQL SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST tasks.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
A DBT_CORE task is present
The task runs the DBT_CORE_EXECUTE job
The dbt command includes a test or build step
dbt's tests are run through the dbt CLI task rather than reimplemented as hand-written SQL SNOWFLAKE_RUN_TEST statements
If both a run/build and a test step are represented, their relative order preserves models being built before tests run against them

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset check, which runs a Great Expectations checkpoint, to Orchestra (see files/ge_checkpoint_check.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live checkpoint runs, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra v1 pipeline YAML with a PYTHON / PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task that runs a script invoking the GE checkpoint and surfaces its pass/fail result via set_outputs, since there is no native Great Expectations integration.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares version v1
A PYTHON task is present
The task runs the PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT job
set_outputs is enabled so the checkpoint's pass/fail reaches Orchestra
No native Great Expectations or pandera integration is invented — the check is run via a Python script rather than a fabricated GE-specific task type
The generated script (or its reference) actually surfaces the checkpoint's success/failure signal, e.g. via client.set_output(...) or a non-zero exit code, rather than always reporting success
